In the pool: sessions may claim this server · on
10.0.0.5:3306 · a session claims this server for itself while it runs
One session holds a server at a time, so the pool is the session cap: as many sessions may be open at once as there are entries in it. The session's project decides
which database name is used on it (created if missing); its setup commands are where migrations and seeding happen, on every session.
2 servers in the pool, so 2 sessions with a database may be open at once. 1 more is listed but taken out of the pool.
Settings · SSH server › SSH server tab
Available to sessions on this project · on
First verify the server's host key and add it to the Briareus account's known_hosts file. Unknown or changed host keys are refused. SSH configuration aliases and
A MySQL login on this server, stored encrypted. Clients reach the database through an SSH tunnel to this server, at the host and port below as the server itself
A login is stored. Type a password only to change it.
Stored · type a new token to replace it
Reference: briareus-windows. Other clients match this structure, differing only as noted here.

Database pool rows show the label (or host:port) over host:port. The section title carries '· N sessions', the pool's capacity. Delete reads 'Remove this server from the pool' and asks 'Remove <name> from the pool?'.
Port is a narrow cell (140px) beside Host. Username and Password share the row equally.
The SSH Database tab is offered only when the server's catalog has GET /settings/ssh/servers/{id}/db-credentials. Otherwise that tab explains the server must be updated.
Forge account has Save and 🗑 only (no clone). A row's dot means a token is stored.

A tab with unsaved changes gets ' •' (for example 'SSH server •', 'Forge account •'). New entries show as 'New database server' / 'New SSH server' / 'New Forge account' with 'not saved yet' in the sidebar, and only Save in the
Region names (sidebar, canvas, raise, sunken) are the theme.* roles; widths and margins are layout.* in tokens/. Greys only, on purpose.
